newsitem.title: USA: Israel peace effort needed for new investment - poll.
newsitem.headline: Israel peace effort needed for new investment - poll.

text.p: Most U.S. business leaders with investments in Israel would not sell their stakes if the peace process collapses, but such a development would keep many of them from increasing their investment there, a survey showed.

The poll of 49 executives, conducted by Yankelovich Partners, found that 57 percent of respondants said problems with the Israeli-Palestinian peace effort have not affected their investment decisions.
But 59 percent said a collapse in the peace process would make Israel a "place to hold, but not expand investments," the survey showed.
Eight percent said Israel would be "as good as ever a place to invest" even if the process, begun with the 1993 Oslo accords, broke down.

"American investors in Israel have soured on (Israeli) Prime Minister Netanyahu's handling of the peace process in recent months and would be unlikely to expand their investments if things get much worse," said a report by the survey's sponsors, the Israel Policy Forum and the Center for Middle East Peace and Economic Cooperation.

"These findings refute those who say that Israel can continue to attract foreign investments without progress in the peace process," Stanley Gold, president of Shamrock Holdings Inc, said in the report.
Gold is chairman of Koor Industries Ltd and vice president of the Israel Policy Forum.
"Many American investors are clearly unhappy with the current state of the peace process and if things get much worse, they are going to look elsewhere for new investment opportunities," Gold said.
Yankelovich Partners is a survey research firm.
